title: the-loop plugin configuration
description: Schema for .the-loop/harness-config.yaml — the HARNESS (plugin) config, installed per repo and read by the /the-loop:* commands and the skill working that repo: the few facts about this repository the agent cannot infer (where the specs live, the instruction docs, the testing conventions, the API contracts, the design artifacts). Layout, tooling and git hooks are inferred from the repository every session; the review-round policy is the operator's cli-config.yaml. THE CLI NEVER READS THIS FILE (issue-352, decision-123): what the CLI needs it takes from its own cli-config.yaml (spec directory, critics, graph hooks) or from flags the agent passes (`--spec-dir`, `--glob`, `--doc`); the skill tells the agent which. Phase labels are `loop:<phase>`, fixed; the ticket's repository is the work item's ref, not a setting.

x-onboarding.description: Drives the guided onboarding `/the-loop:init` runs (see the the-loop skill's reference/onboarding.md). Groups club related top-level keys that interact and are established with the user together, in this order. Per-key explanations, defaults, enum possibilities and examples come from the property schemas below — this block only adds grouping and ask policy, so the schema stays the single source of truth. `version` belongs to no group: init stamps it. A group may carry no key (`people`): it exists to establish a sibling file. Repository layout and tooling are not groups any more: the skill infers them from the repository every session (issue-352). Validators ignore x-* keywords.

askLevels.always: No sensible default exists — init MUST establish this group with the user (or report it under needs-user when running non-interactively).
askLevels.confirm: Init proposes sensible values (detected from the repo, else the schema default) and asks the user to confirm or adjust the whole group in one pass.
askLevels.advanced: Sensible defaults are applied silently; the group is only walked through when the user asks for the full tour.

groups.title: Custom instructions
groups.explain: Per-installation instruction documents (readme/markdown files) the harness reads and honors while working: team conventions, developing/testing/coding styles, house rules the structured config does not model. Candidates are detected from common convention files (CONTRIBUTING.md, docs style guides); supplementary to the external-tools registry.

groups.title: Workflow & phases
groups.explain: Where the-loop's checked-in knowledge lives in this repository (specs, capability docs, learnings). Phase labels are fixed (`loop:<phase>`); if specDir moves, the CLI's routing.graph.specDir moves with it.

groups.title: Testing conventions
groups.explain: Gherkin scenario docstrings on integration tests, requirement links, and the integration-test globs the agent hands to `the-loop scenarios --glob`. What runs before a commit or push is the repository's own hook manager (or lint, typecheck and unit tests when it has none) and is inferred, not configured (issue-352).

groups.title: People & interaction
groups.explain: Who approves work: collaborators (people, roles) live in .the-loop/collaborators.yaml (collaborators.schema.json) — init establishes that file in this group; it holds no harness-config key. Every decision needs a paper trail, so at least one approver role must resolve to a person. How the harness presents work to humans (mermaid diagrams, the PR briefing, the the-loop:writing contract) is fixed since issue-352.

groups.title: API contracts & design artifacts
groups.explain: Contract-first API specs (OpenAPI/GraphQL) and how UI/UX design artifacts are captured in the design phase. Only relevant to projects exposing an API or a user-facing surface.

version.description: Schema version of this config file. Used by /upgrade-the-loop to reconcile. 0.3.0 (issue-352) removed ticketing, workflow.phases/phaseLabelPrefix/specApproach/requireHumanReviewPerPhase, localOrchestration, notifications, reviews.critics and graph — see the upgrade command for where each went. It also removed autonomy, security, tdd, minimalism, tokenEconomy, selfImprovement, contextManagement, userInteraction and externalTools: those configured what is now simply the loop's rule (risk tiers, security gates, TDD, minimalism, token economy, learnings, context management, the writing contract) and the harness discovers its own tools. A third pass removed repository, tooling, hooks and observability (the skill infers layout, tooling and git hooks from the repository; logging is the project's own) and moved reviews to the CLI config's top-level `reviews`.

workflow.description: The Kiro-style 3-phase spec workflow (plus the testing plan) and where the-loop's checked-in knowledge lives in this repository. The phases themselves are the process graph's (shipped with the CLI) and the ticket labels are `loop:<phase>`; neither is configured here since issue-352.

specDir.description: Per-work-item spec files live in <specDir>/<id>/{requirements|bugfix,design,testing-plan,tasks,execution-log}.md. The AGENT's key: the CLI resolves the same directory from its own `routing.graph.specDir` (default docs/specs) or `--spec-dir`, so a repository that moves its specs sets both (issue-352).

capabilitiesDir.description: Living capability docs (the organized view of specs; single source of truth for a capability's current behaviour) live in <capabilitiesDir>/, indexed by <capabilitiesDir>/capabilities.md. Affected docs are updated in the same PR as the work item (ready-to-ship gate item).

learningsDir.description: The learnings tree the self-improvement lifecycle maintains: the injected index <learningsDir>/learnings.md, one <learningsDir>/learning-<nnn>.md per durable learning, and the consolidated overflow in <learningsDir>/topics/<category>.md. Tuned by `selfImprovement`; the git-ignored write-gate queue stays under .the-loop/learnings-pending/ and is not affected by this key. Repo-relative, like specDir and capabilitiesDir. NOTE that the default places learnings inside the documentation tree: a project that PUBLISHES docs/ and would rather not publish its learnings should point this key somewhere it does not build from.

customInstructions.description: User-provided instruction documents the harness reads and honors while working this repo/workspace: readme/markdown files carrying team conventions, developing/testing/coding styles and house rules the structured config does not model. Per-installation — each installation of the-loop points at its own docs via configurable paths. Supplementary to externalTools (that registers tools the harness may use; this registers guidance it must follow). Load order, precedence and limits: reference/instructions.md.

docs.description: Ordered list of instruction documents, read in order when starting work on a work item (later docs win over earlier ones where they conflict).

examples.notes: House TS style, naming, PR etiquette.

path.description: Path to a markdown/readme instruction file. Repo-relative, or absolute for per-machine docs living outside the repo (e.g. a company-wide conventions file).

notes.description: What the doc covers / when it matters, so phase-scoped loading knows when to (re-)read it.

onMissing.description: What to do when a configured doc does not exist at its path: warn = note it in the execution log and continue; error = stop and ask the user; ignore = skip silently.

testing.description: Integration-test scenario conventions and how the harness queries them. See reference/testing.md.

gherkinDocstrings.description: RULE: every integration test carries a Gherkin-syntax docstring (Feature/Scenario/Given-When-Then) naming the scenario under test.

linkRequirements.description: When a test is tied to a requirements.md, its docstring includes a `Requirement:` link to that file (and section anchor).

integrationTestGlobs.description: Globs the harness scans to enumerate integration-test scenarios (`the-loop scenarios`). Empty = use the CLI's built-in defaults.

apiSpecs.description: Where API contracts are authored and how docs are generated from them. See reference/testing.md (API specs).

dir.description: RULE: all RESTful API specs are authored here in the OpenAPI format.

generateDocs.description: Documentation is generated automatically from the OpenAPI specs.

docsTool.description: Tool that renders docs from OpenAPI. Free-form; e.g. redocly, widdershins, swagger-ui.

graphql.description: GraphQL best practice: an SDL-first schema, checked in, linted/snapshot-tested, and documented.

dir.description: Where the checked-in GraphQL schema lives.

schemaFormat.description: Schema Definition Language — the human-authored, checked-in, snapshot-tested contract.

generateDocs.description: Documentation is generated automatically from the SDL schema.

docsTool.description: Tool that renders docs from the SDL. Free-form; e.g. spectaql, graphdoc, magidoc.

design.description: How UI/UX (visual) design is captured and iterated in the design phase, alongside design.md's architecture/HLD/LLD. See reference/design-artifacts.md.

uiArtifacts.description: Visual design artifacts for work items with a user-facing surface. First-class, tracked design-phase artifacts (siblings of design.md), iterated-until-locked with the designer persona and referenced from the ticket. Work items with no UI simply produce none.

dir.description: Directory (relative to the work item's spec dir, <specDir>/<id>/) holding checked-in UI/UX design artifacts, e.g. docs/specs/<id>/design/.

format.description: Preferred representation for generated visual design: self-contained HTML+CSS+JS prototypes (Claude-artifact style), a linked Figma file, or both.

selfContained.description: RULE for HTML prototypes: self-contained (inline CSS/JS, data-URI assets, no external network deps) so they render standalone in a browser and as a Claude-style artifact.

screenshotEvidence.description: Capture rendered screenshots of the locked design artifacts as design-phase evidence, embedded in the reviewer briefing.
